mcqs.question: In logical statements, the implication "If P then Q" is best described as:

options.A: P is true only when Q is true
options.B: If P is true then Q must be true
options.C: Q is true only if P is false
options.D: Both P and Q are always true

mcqs.answer: If P is true then Q must be true
mcqs.explanation: An implication P → Q is true in all cases except when P is true and Q is false. Hence it means that whenever P holds, Q must also hold. Option A confuses implication with equivalence, C is unrelated, and D is incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following represents the biconditional relationship between statements P and Q?

options.C: P and Q are both true or both false
options.D: Either P or Q but not both

mcqs.answer: P and Q are both true or both false
mcqs.explanation: The biconditional P ↔ Q is true exactly when P and Q have the same truth value – both true or both false. Options A and B are one‑way implications, while D describes exclusive OR.

mcqs.question: For the compound statement (P ∧ Q) → ¬R, what is its truth value when P = True, Q = False, and R = False?
mcqs.explanation: P ∧ Q = True ∧ False = False. An implication with a false antecedent is always true, regardless of the consequent ¬R (which is True). Hence the whole statement is True. Options B‑D are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly represents the conjunction of "It is raining" (P) and "The ground is wet" (Q)?

options.A: If it is raining then the ground is wet
options.B: The ground is wet only if it is raining
options.C: It is raining and the ground is wet
options.D: Either it is raining or the ground is wet

mcqs.answer: It is raining and the ground is wet
mcqs.explanation: Conjunction (P ∧ Q) asserts that both component statements are true simultaneously. Option C states exactly that. Options A and B are implications, while D is a disjunction.

mcqs.question: The logical disjunction P ∨ Q is true when:

options.A: Both P and Q are false
options.B: Exactly one of P or Q is true
options.C: At least one of P or Q is true
options.D: Both P and Q are true only

mcqs.answer: At least one of P or Q is true
mcqs.explanation: Disjunction in logic is inclusive: it is true if P is true, Q is true, or both are true. Option B describes exclusive OR, A is false, and D misstates the condition.

mcqs.question: If the implication P → Q is false, which of the following must be true?

options.A: P is true and Q is false
options.B: P is false and Q is true
options.C: Both P and Q are true
options.D: Both P and Q are false

mcqs.answer: P is true and Q is false
mcqs.explanation: An implication is false only in the case where the antecedent P is true while the consequent Q is false. All other combinations make the implication true. Hence option A is the only possibility.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is equivalent to the biconditional P ↔ Q?
mcqs.explanation: A biconditional is true when P and Q have the same truth value. This can be expressed as the conjunction of two implications (A) or as the disjunction of both being true or both being false (B). Hence both are equivalent to P ↔ Q.

mcqs.question: For how many of the eight possible truth assignments of P, Q, R is the statement (P ∨ Q) ∧ (¬P ∨ R) true?
mcqs.explanation: Evaluating all eight combinations shows the statement is true for (T,T,T), (T,F,T), (F,T,T), and (F,T,F) – a total of four cases. Options A, B, and D are therefore incorrect.
